questions.q: What does the 'fanning in' pattern described in this lesson actually set up?
options: One independent Auto Loader stream per source table, each with its own schema location and checkpoint
A single stream that reads every source table through one shared checkpoint
A batch job that runs once per day instead of streaming at all
A single table that merges every source into one undifferentiated schema
questions.explain: Fanning in means running one Auto Loader stream per source table independently, scaling Lesson 10's single-stream pattern out to a whole bronze layer.

questions.q: Why does checkpoint naming discipline matter at the scale of a dozen streams?
options: Losing track of which checkpoint belongs to which stream can cause double-processing or a silently stalled table
Checkpoint names have no functional effect at any scale
Only one checkpoint is ever needed regardless of how many streams exist
Checkpoints are automatically renamed by Unity Catalog if they conflict
questions.explain: Predictable, paired naming for schema-location and stream checkpoints avoids the real risk of misapplied checkpoints across tables.

questions.q: What is the real cost of choosing many small per-table streams over one multiplexed stream?
options: More clusters/jobs running, a real cost and monitoring surface, in exchange for fault isolation
There is no real cost — many small streams are strictly better in every case
Many small streams cannot use checkpoints at all
Many small streams require abandoning Auto Loader entirely
questions.explain: Many small streams trade more operational overhead for the benefit that a failure in one table never touches another.

questions.q: What is the real risk of one big multiplexed stream handling every source table?
options: One bad file or schema break in any single table can stall ingestion for every table at once
It always costs more to run than many small streams
It cannot use trigger(processingTime=...) at all
It requires file notification mode specifically
questions.explain: A shared pipeline means a single table's failure can block processing for all the other tables riding along in the same stream.

questions.q: According to this lesson, is there one universally 'correct' ingestion topology for Auto Loader at scale?
options: No — it's a real trade-off sized to how many sources exist and how independently they fail
Yes — many small streams are always the correct choice
Yes — one multiplexed stream is always the correct choice
Topology choice has no measurable effect on a production pipeline
questions.explain: This lesson's honest close is that the choice depends on real factors like fault isolation needs and operational overhead tolerance, not a fixed rule.
